exposure: mode of birth (vaginal without vacuum extraction, vacuum extraction, acute caesarean section)
support from a trusted birth companion
outcome: childbirth experience (overall satisfaction, Own Capacity, Perceived Safety, Professional Support, Participation)
cohort: The study participants were 619 postnatal Swedish women who answered a digital survey six to 16 weeks postpartum.
finding: The study found that several factors, including a vaginal mode of birth without vacuum extraction, absence of ongoing mental health problems, no maternal complications postpartum, and strong birth companion support, contributed to a positive childbirth experience.
mod_finding: Having a vaginal mode of birth (without vacuum extraction) was a major factor influencing a positive total childbirth experience, with the study advocating for birth approaches that optimize vaginal birth over vacuum extraction or acute caesarean section.
